title: Total knockout (almost)
body:
This app and it’s many features are a great way to keep track of your daily chores/activities. 
It has a really neat design thats just super intuitive. No extra pages of useless information, plus you can move your ideas/list items around with ease.
It’s got great ways of keeping you reminded of your responsibilities, one of which being the home screen widgets. 

However-
Don’t get me wrong I absolutely love everything about this app but theres always room for improvement. Namely the widgets; for example, the 4 space square one that reads what you have on in the selected list… I feel like it’d be more useful if the item listed would scroll through instead of stay on just the one. 
Little things I know but I figured it’d be cool. 
Or another idea, perhaps, which was a big deal for me; the “assigned to me” section. I get that it’s more of a school/work related feature, but having a way to make it more accessible for all users would be awesome, say I want my wife to get me something from the shops; a shared list section would do wonders. 
These little feature ideas far from degrade the experience of this awesome app. Overall it’s been a real big use in my daily life and I always highly recommend it to any newcomers looking for an ‘easy to use’ app, for your day to day.

title: Missing feature
body:
This is a great little app except for 1 glaring/annoying aspect. We use it for our joint shopping list…either person can add items & then when someone goes shopping they instantly see a completely up-to-date list of what’s needed. We have something like 150 items in the groceries list that we’ve bought at some time and we simply unstick when needed again. 
The problem is when walking around the supermarket with the list open virtually any accidental touch of the screen will tick (or untick) an item. AND YOU USUALLY HAVE NO IDEA WHAT’S GONE MISSING!
In the old days when “Sort” was something you had to initiate manually, this wasn’t much of a problem, as the newly ticked item would be sitting at the top, and you could untick it again. But now that it instantly sorts, one doesn’t know!  
We need an “Undo” option, or “Show last 3 actions”, or some other way of recovering. 
Please.

title: Caution: late adopters beware
body:
Apple hardware can be long-lived. For those of us who rarely buy new iphones, there's a risk your version of this app may stop working reliably, with loss of data. 

As we know, developers stop maintaining an app on one platform but the old version keeps working. I still have an old version of iOS (12) with an old, once usable version (2.40) of this app.

I'd used the app for years and watched it get bloated. However I'd got used to keeping not just todo lists but long lists of other info in it because I'd liked the interface.

A couple of years ago I got messages from the developers to upgrade urgently to a new version or risk losing data but whenever I tried to, the App Store kept insisting I already had the latest version.  Besides the iphone, I had it on 2 computers running different OS versions and the App Store said the same about all of them. When the ultimatum in the warnings expired I still hadn't solved this.

After that the app still appeared to work OK. Only over time did I see that new data on each device had not been syncing with others! I contacted MS and they said, just get a new iphone.

When I want to write something the iphone's usually at hand and I kept using this one on it alone while Iooked for another app I liked. Gradually it got unreliable with even that. The last straw was when I deleted a word from one entry in a list and just lost the whole list.

At last I've discovered the free bare-bones app that does what I want reliably: Apple's Reminders. Now how to get all data I still have into it? The only export function available is to another (commercial) MS product and...

To Do dislikes:

• Too many steps involved in setting a custom reminder day & time.

• Can’t subscribe to calendar (task reminders sync with iOS calendar).  
• Too many steps to view completed tasks and they show up amongst incomplete tasks.  
• Moving a Step to the List has too many press-and-hold actions. Could add to the List when the List name flashes, instead of waiting til the List opens - which is fine for moving to other List).

• Font styling on Main screen is awful (it’s nice within Lists). And can’t change theme/background.  
• Not much Smart List customisation in settings

title: A disappointing replacement for Wunderlist
body:
Works fine providing you don’t want to share a list with someone. If you do, this rather bizarrely insists that you can’t do it unless they’re from the same organisation as you, or you both have exactly the same type of Microsoft account. 

So if, like me, you’ve been forced to switch to this app because Wunderlist doesn’t exist anymore, and you only ever used Wunderlist to share shopping lists with your partner, AND both of your Microsoft accounts are work-related when your Wunderlist ones weren’t, this app is pointless for you. 

It’s a very strange “feature” to adopt when that essentially cripples the potential user base for To Do. Even if you’re not switching from Wunderlist, which had no such restrictions and just worked, why would anyone want there to be a restriction on who they could use this with, when there’s no benefit to there being one?

As such, this is a good app that is totally useless to me now and I’ll be looking to replace it, when I’d only ever gotten it to replace an app I was previously happy with.

This is a key standout compared to other todo apps, where you end up with an overflowing list of overdue tasks that becomes unmanageable and you end up ignoring things and missing the important stuff.

The other unique feature is the ability to flag emails in Outlook and they’re converted to tasks in their own list. This integration is a killer feature; emails I need to action, I just flag and bam task created.

Whilst you can create steps for a task, the only issue for me is you can’t create sub-tasks in a hierarchical way. Add this and it’s perfect.

title: Why not just rebadge Wunderlist? This app is a poor alternative
body:

For MS Office 365 subscribers this would have been a great way to improve cross platform computing options (given how well Wunderlist had achieved cross platform functionality), and also advertise MS as being more consumer friendly.
Unfortunately this resulting MS taskmanager is a poor alternative. Many of the things which made Wunderlist great are missing. Having tried it briefly I have now switched with some reservations to Google keep. At least I can share tasks and add images to reminders/checklists
As with MS Outlook and the acquisition of Sunrise calendars for iOS, the initial development looked promising, however the many requested features (via their in app feedback option) go unanswered - ultimately for years. Why is this the case when they have already acquired a product which has these features buit in??
Look elsewhere for an app with significant ongoing development.
